_comment: Aelgard Veilwood bestiary. Moonlit woodland, mirror-glass beasts, elven patrols, fey spirits. Tone: quiet, slow-breathing, unwelcoming to noise. Threats here punish casting spells out loud and blundering.
_region_tone: moonlit quiet, antler-shadow, an unsettled neutrality. The forest is not hostile; it is negotiating.

monsters.name: Mirror stag
bible: Mirror stags have antlers of fused mirror-glass instead of bone. Nobody knows the metabolic pathway. The antlers reflect a slightly delayed image of whatever they face — by a second, not more, but enough to put an attacker one step behind.

A hunter who looks a mirror stag in the antler sees himself in the position he was in a heartbeat ago. Experienced Veilwood hunters teach apprentices to strike at the tail rather than the head for this reason.
The antler fragments retain the delay property when cut, which makes them valuable in reflection-based optical arts.
monsters.habitat: moonlit glades, the Antler-Path rings, glass-deer herds in the northern wood
monsters.reagent_callout: Mirror-deer antler (1/8) — reagent for Second-Thought helm (once per combat, resists a fatal hit and applies heal-over-time).

monsters.name: Glass spider
monsters.examine: Its web cuts. Its bite sings.
bible: Glass spiders spin webs of translucent silica-silk. The silk is strong, nearly invisible, and razor-edged when rolled taut. Walking into a glass-spider web in daylight is how most Veilwood hikers lose a season of crossings.
The spider drops from its web onto its target. Once on the ground it is slower than a caster can react, so the danger is precisely the drop, not the chase.
Silk harvested fresh winds onto a bow-tiller to make the Veilwood's best ranger strings.
monsters.habitat: canopy webs, moonlight corridors, the Long Ride
monsters.reagent_callout: Glass-spider silk (1/6) — reagent for glassprint bowstring (Veilwood ranger-tier).

monsters.name: Veil warden
monsters.examine: Elven. Patrol. Watches first. Shoots second.
bible: Veil wardens are the regular patrol force of the elven council. They walk the major paths in pairs, with elk-hide cloaks and a regulation longbow. They are passive; they will not initiate combat unless the trespass is gross.
Their draw is fast enough that a provoked warden can arrow a caster before the casting completes. Do not provoke them.
They accept diplomatic tokens — the Veilwood writ, available from the council-clerk in Glimwood — and will escort the holder safely through even contested zones.
monsters.habitat: elven patrol-paths, the Long Ride, Glimwood approaches
monsters.anti_pattern_note: Veilwood writ fully bypasses aggro. Encounters that spawn wardens on a writ-holding player are incorrect.

monsters.name: Moonlight panther
monsters.examine: Part cat, part moonlight, all appetite.
bible: Moonlight panthers are cats of exceptionally pale fur with a faint self-luminosity visible at full moon. They hunt at night and are essentially invisible in fog.

A panther always hunts alone but shares territory with its kin — adjacent ranges, never overlapping. A Veilwood ranger can map the panther territories by moonrise signals: panthers yowl once each at moonrise to announce 'still here' to neighbours.
Their pelt is highly prized; a full moonlight pelt is the material for the Veilwood elven nobility's winter cloaks.
monsters.habitat: glades at night, fog-filled valleys, moonrise-calling clearings
monsters.reagent_callout: Moonlight pelt (1/24) — reagent for moonlit cloak (stealth rating + night-vision in Veilwood).

monsters.name: Corrupted dryad
monsters.examine: A dryad whose tree was felled. She didn't take it well.
bible: Each dryad is bound to a specific tree. When the tree is felled — even by legitimate authority — the dryad does not die; she is liberated into wandering, and the liberation is a corruption.
A corrupted dryad hunts anyone who touches bark. This includes foresters, furniture-carvers, and hikers with a walking-stick. She is especially relentless against chippers and sawyers.
She can be put to rest only by planting a new tree — not just any tree, but a seedling from her original tree, which must have survived. Most have not.
monsters.habitat: old-growth stumps, Sawmill Row, logging-camp outskirts
monsters.reagent_callout: Corrupted acorn (1/12) — reagent for the 'Replant' one-shot consumable (removes a corrupted dryad from the world state for 30 days in-game).

monsters.name: Veilgrove hag
monsters.examine: A tree-witch with a dangerous hospitality.
bible: Veilgrove hags live in cottages camouflaged as giant tree-stumps. They are expert hosts; they will invite a traveller in, offer tea, and, if the traveller stays past the third cup, cook him.

The tea is real. The conversation is educational. Veilgrove hags are a valuable source of old-dialect lore, and a foolish player who stays too long does gain permanent +1 herblore skill -- and then dies.
A hag will not chase beyond her cottage. The rule is old. It is etched inside the doorway.
monsters.habitat: hollow-stump cottages, deep Veilwood interior off the patrol paths
monsters.anti_pattern_note: hospitality phase is a real mechanic. First interaction = conversation, NOT combat. Combat only triggers if the player drinks three cups.

monsters.name: Spore drake
monsters.examine: A dragon-kin with fungus for scales.
bible: Spore drakes are Veilwood-adapted dragons. Their scales have been colonised by native fungi over many generations, to the point that the drake and its scale-mycelia are a symbiotic organism. The fungus provides temperature regulation and a spore-cloud attack; the dragon provides mobility.
A spore drake exhales a cloud of mind-altering spores at mid-range. Characters inhaling the cloud experience short hallucinations (non-damaging but disorienting, reducing accuracy for 30 seconds).
A mask, ironically from the Sootworks air-quality program, fully blocks the spore effect. Cross-regional gear matters.
monsters.habitat: deep Veilwood mycelium-ridden thickets, the Spore Ring
monsters.reagent_callout: Spore-drake mycelium (1/20) — reagent for mycelium dust (thrown consumable, 30s confusion vs any magic-tag mob).

monsters.name: Fey knight
monsters.examine: Heavy armor of hawthorn and silver. Oaths keep it moving.
bible: Fey knights are sworn to the Winter Court of the Veilwood and ride out only on specific nights of the year — the equinoxes, the solstices, and the midpoint between. They carry hawthorn-branch lances bound with silver and ride stags, not horses.
A fey knight will ignore any traveller not carrying iron. Iron offends the Court. Iron weapons provoke immediate challenge.
A knight's gauntlet is valuable as a diplomatic token in Heartlands-elven negotiations; every gauntlet is signed by the knight.
monsters.habitat: equinox-road, solstice-tracks, the four ceremonial fey patrols
monsters.anti_pattern_note: iron-carrier aggro is REAL. Player wearing iron gear in Veilwood during solstice window gets auto-aggro'd.

monsters.name: Heartwood treant
monsters.examine: A tree older than the Heartlands. It knows.
bible: Heartwood treants are the oldest living things in Aelgard. Each is a tree that has accumulated, over four to six centuries, sufficient arboreal consciousness to speak. They do not move unless disturbed; they speak in long vowels and understand all major human tongues.
A passive treant will trade old lore — quest hints, regional histories — in exchange for a single young sapling planted nearby. This is a genuine respected exchange.

Disturbing a treant is a crime in elven law. Killing one is an unresolved offence — the elves will not prosecute, but the Veilwood itself remembers, and the forest becomes hostile to the killer for a lunar cycle.
monsters.habitat: the Old Grove interior, specifically six named sites (Oakfather, Second-Mother, etc.)
monsters.anti_pattern_note: passive. Attacking a treant without quest authority triggers region-wide Veilwood aggro debuff for 30 days in-game.

monsters.name: Pixie swarm
monsters.examine: Six to ten pixies having opinions.
bible: A pixie is not a tier of creature but a term for small fey who have not yet chosen a Court. Swarms form around a grievance — a broken fence, a wanton harvest, a loud traveller — and disperse when the grievance is addressed.
They sting, they pull hair, they steal small shiny objects and return most of them within the hour. Pixie-swarm encounters feel inconvenient more than dangerous.
They cannot be bargained with, but they can be distracted: a handful of dropped copper coins will hold their attention for ten minutes, which is enough to pass through.
monsters.habitat: any grievance-inducing act near Veilwood boundaries, especially the fence at Glimwood-edge
monsters.reagent_callout: Moonpetal (1/4) — reagent for the minor restoration potion (25% HP, Veilwood variant).

monsters.name: Glimstalker
monsters.examine: Made of twilight. Hunts by scent of intention.
bible: Glimstalkers are predators of the twilight band — the half-hour before dusk and the half-hour after dawn. They are hunters of intention: they detect, at distance, the mental pre-commitment to an action. A hunter preparing to shoot has committed the intention; a hiker deciding between paths has not.
Their hide is barely visible in twilight, perfectly invisible in dusk proper. The elven rangers hunt them by reading the ground-pattern of bent grass where a glimstalker has passed.
A player who goes still of mind — meditates, sits — becomes invisible to a glimstalker. This is a teachable technique; the elven council teaches it in a mid-game quest.
monsters.habitat: twilight-band paths, specifically the Glimwood-Old Grove corridor
monsters.anti_pattern_note: pre-commit intention detection is a real mechanic. Player in still-mode (no queued actions) is invisible.

monsters.name: Grotto nymph
monsters.examine: Bound to a pool. Will drown a fool. Will trade for pearls.
bible: Each Veilwood spring has a nymph attached. She is not hostile unless the spring is fouled. She bargains: pearl-for-pearl trades with travellers for fresh-water charms, minor healing, and, rarely, access to hidden dive-routes.
A nymph's drowning is legal only in defence of her spring. She will absolutely drown a pollutor.
Nymphs communicate across springs by underground seepage; an insult at one pool carries to all pools by nightfall.
monsters.habitat: every Veilwood spring (nine named springs), particularly the Moss-Ring, Lady's-Foot, and Second-Mother springs
monsters.anti_pattern_note: passive. Killing a nymph bans the player from ALL Veilwood springs for 90 days in-game; quest failure cascades.

monsters.name: Old wolf queen
monsters.examine: She was a queen. Wolves remember.
bible: An Old Wolf Queen is a wolf that has ruled a pack for three generations — an improbable feat. Only two exist in the current Veilwood population: the North Queen (pack of eleven) and the Moon-Valley Queen (pack of eight).
She fights as a pack, never alone. Attacking her alone provokes the whole pack within 40 paces.
Her pelt, hung in a home, is said to ward off all wolves for a generation — which is empirically true; wolves will detour the house miles out of their way.
monsters.habitat: the North Ridge and Moon-Valley pack territories
monsters.reagent_callout: Wolf queen pelt (1/48 collection-log) — reagent for the wolf-ward hearth charm (housing upgrade: -50% aggro from all wolf-tag within 20 tiles of player home).

region_flavor_drops: Wolf queen pelt (1/48 collection-log — reagent: wolf-ward hearth charm)
